messages:
tara (design): Quick design riff 1: what if playback had a "pause-on-hover" affordance for the rule canvas? lets people inspect long rules while sim runs. pros/cons?

yusuf (pm): pause-on-hover is neat but might be unexpected for keyboard users. need an explicit toggle in the rail or a hotkey (space?) to pause/resume.

hannah (frontend): technically doable. hover semantics are tricky for touch. fallback: hover pauses on pointer devices, and a visible 'Pause' button in the legend for touch/keyboard.

jade (a11y): hover-only behavior is not accessible. Keyboard users need a control and we need to expose the state via `aria-pressed` or `aria-checked`. Also avoid magic hover that changes layout focus unexpectedly.

mike (research): From test sessions, people appreciated being able to freeze playback to read long conditions. They preferred an explicit affordance because hover sometimes caused accidental freezes.

tara (design): OK so: show a small pause/play toggle in the left rail, keep hover as a nicety on desktop but not the only mechanism. Also want to experiment with a 'step' control to move one rule at a time.

hannah (frontend): step control doable: `Step Forward` / `Step Back` actions. We'll wire keyboard shortcuts: `.` and `,` (like media keys). Need to publish shortcuts in a help panel.

jade (a11y): Publish shortcuts in the help panel and expose them in the rail via a small tooltip. For screen reader users, include an accessible command list dialog (`role=dialog`) reachable from the rail.

yusuf (pm): Another UX decision: where to show validation severities during simulation? Inline badges? colored left border? a combined panel?

tara (design): My preference is inline severity chips under rule title (error/warning/info) + a small left-most colored stripe for glanceability. But must ensure non-color cues exist.

jade (a11y): Yes: colored stripe + icon + text. And each chip should have `aria-label` like "Error: missing condition". Avoid using only icons without text.

mike (research): note: in usability tests some users skim for numeric priority not color. Consider numbering priorities and showing severity as an icon cluster separate from priority.

hannah (frontend): we'll render priority as a numeric chip (1/2/3) and have a separate small severity cluster (⚠️ ! ✓). For the colored stripe, ensure CSS uses `outline` styles that don't get lost behind the drag placeholder.

tara (design): drag placeholder: current ghost pushes other rules down and reflows which makes it hard to watch sim while dragging. Proposal: use an overlay ghost that floats above the list and leaves layout stable.

hannah (frontend): floating ghost is more work but much nicer. We can add `aria-grabbed` states and ensure keyboard move actions animate without reflow. For touch, long-press starts float.

jade (a11y): Ensure `aria-dropeffect` / `aria-grabbed` patterns are used and provide alternative move up/down buttons for non-drag users. Also make the ghost visible to assistive tech via `aria-hidden=false` and a short announce like "Moving rule X".

yusuf (pm): copy: prefer action-first microcopy. For validation chips use: "Missing match 1" vs "Rule missing match condition"? keeps length short but still clear.

mike (research): test favoring: short + actionable. e.g., "Missing match 1" plus an inline link "Add" works well.

tara (design): mobile: rail becomes hidden under an icon. snapshot and pause controls should be available in the header for small screens. Also snapshot should include a lightweight timeline so users can inspect the moment they captured.

hannah (frontend): timeline mini-strip is feasible: small thumbnails + timestamp. Be mindful of storage; snapshots are pointers to run state not full copies. We'll redact content by default.

jade (a11y): timeline thumbnails need alt text and keyboard nav. Also avoid very small touch targets. If thumbnails are tiny, provide a list view alternative.

yusuf (pm): security: ensure snapshots don't persist PII by default and add a toggle 'Include values' protected by extra confirmation.

ui-bot: prototype updated: https://figma.redwood.design/proto/pause-step-rail - added pause toggle, step controls, floating drag ghost, and severity chips (comments open).

tara (design): Nice. Final questions for action items: what should default keyboard shortcut for pause be? space conflicts with textareas. maybe `k` like video players?

jade (a11y): choose a non-conflicting single-key shortcut but always document it and allow users to remap via the help dialog. Make sure shortcuts don't trigger while typing in inputs. Use `Ctrl+Alt+K` as a safer default for power users.

hannah (frontend): I'll implement `Ctrl+Alt+K` as default and add optional `k` if the global state is clear and focus not in a text field. Also add an explicit button in the rail.

yusuf (pm): Action items: Hannah implement pause/step/ghost + keyboard hook; Jade write a11y checklist for aria-live, drag states, shortcuts; Tara update mocks with timeline + mobile header; Mike will run a small follow-up usability test after flag rollout. Ship behind feature flag.

tara (design): thanks team 1 we'll review the PR in design-sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
